Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

apparently adverb

as it seems

also seemingly, it seems, it would seem, by the look of it

classical

Plaut. Am. 333: Hinc enim mihi dextra vōx aurīs, ut vidētur, verberat.
Ter. Hec. 272b: Nunc quidem ut vidētur

ut vidētur

parenthesis: ut with the third person of videor

apparently, as it seems

Set into the sentence like English “apparently”, without changing its construction; ut mihi vidētur is “as I see it”. For one’s own guess, ut opīnor (see think).

Other words

  • videor, vidērī, vīsus sum — seem, appear (to be or to do)

    verb, second conjugation, passive, with a nominative and infinitive · also used · classical

    Latin turns the adverb into the verb: “apparently he is ill” is aeger esse vidētur, “he seems to be ill” (see seem).

Examples

  • Certumne est istuc? — Nunc quidem ut vidētur.

    Is that settled, then? — For now, apparently.Ter. Hec. 272–272b

  • Hinc enim mihi dextra vōx aurīs, ut vidētur, verberat.

    Yes, a voice is beating on my ears from the right, apparently.Plaut. Am. 333

See also seem, apparently, obviously, think.
